title_vi: Các loại cơ sở dữ liệu khác nhau ở lời hứa: giao dịch, lược đồ và cách mở rộng

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a partial clone of the source repository; git hash-object of the retrieved body matches the source-map blob. No source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Sáu loại cơ sở dữ liệu và câu tóm tắt của từng loại.
Các mô hình dữ liệu xếp cùng một dữ liệu theo nhiều cách.
Khi giao dịch trải qua nhiều dịch vụ: saga và giao dịch bù.
Thử từng chữ của ACID trên PostgreSQL.

claims.evidence: The Azure Architecture Center page Understand data models, the PostgreSQL 16 tutorial on transactions (advanced.sgml) and the Redis transactions page were read from clones of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center, postgres/postgres and redis/docs at pinned commits; the transfer and schema results were measured by the author, who ran them on PostgreSQL 16.15 and Redis 7.0.15 with psycopg 3.3.6 and redis-py 8.1.0 on 2026-10-18.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: Relational stores use schema-on-write and support ACID multi-row transactions, and horizontal scale generally requires sharding or partitioning; document stores are schema on read with atomicity per document; key-value stores are schema on read with atomicity per single key and list linear scalability as a strength; strict multi-entity transactions point to relational.
claims.section: Relational data stores; Key-value data stores; Comparative characteristics; Choose among models
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036.

claims.claim_vi: A transaction bundles multiple steps into a single all-or-nothing operation; if a failure prevents it from completing, none of the steps affect the database.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: Errors after EXEC are not handled specially: all other queued commands run even if one fails; Redis does not support rollbacks because it would hurt simplicity and performance; WATCH makes EXEC abort the whole transaction if a watched key changed.
claims.section: Errors inside a transaction; What about rollbacks?; Optimistic locking using check-and-set
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of redis/docs at commit 3b030c7ef066c0bb7f88ddec02c784e49783b0f8.

claims.claim_vi: All commands in a Redis transaction are serialized and executed sequentially as a single isolated operation; a request from another client is never served in the middle of it.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of redis/docs at commit 3b030c7ef066c0bb7f88ddec02c784e49783b0f8.

claims.claim_vi: Measured: moving 100 from a (500) to b with a failing second step: in PostgreSQL, b = 0 and the amount was passed as the text 'một trăm', and the transaction left a = 500, b = 0; in Redis, b held the string 'không phải số', and a MULTI/EXEC block left a = 400 with b unchanged (EXEC returned 400 and 'value is not an integer or out of range'); a quantity 'hai' was rejected by an int column on write, accepted by a jsonb column (with a row missing the field) and failed only when a query summed it, and was accepted by a Redis hash.
claims.verified_by: The author ran and measured this on 2026-10-18 on PostgreSQL 16.15 and Redis 7.0.15.

claims.claim_vi: The source states: Understanding database types means considering key characteristics, popular options and use cases of each type.

design_notes_vi: Ba câu hỏi về lời hứa, hai thử nghiệm (chuyển tiền hỏng giữa chừng, số lượng sai kiểu) và bốn ghi chú đọc kết quả. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source text is a single sentence and the rest is an image the lesson does not reuse; the lesson compares database types by what they promise (atomic scope, where the schema is checked, how they scale) instead of listing them.
Two of the three promises are measured on PostgreSQL and Redis; the scaling promise is taken from the Azure guide.
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
